examples.en: My younger sibling slurps down the noodles in no time.

examples.ko: 국물을 먼저 후루룩한 다음에 건더기를 먹어요.
examples.en: I slurp the broth first and then eat the solid ingredients.
The child slurped the seaweed soup and was startled.

examples.ko: 면을 후루룩할 때 나는 소리가 너무 커요.
examples.en: The sound you make when slurping noodles is really loud.
I was hungry, so I slurped up the porridge in one go.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 차를 후루룩하지 말고 천천히 마셔요.
examples.en: Don't slurp the hot tea; drink it slowly.

explain: '후루룩 마시다/먹다'처럼 부사 '후루룩'에 다른 동사를 붙여 쓰는 말이 더 자연스러워요. 국수나 국물을 소리를 내며 빨리 들이마실 때 써요. 조용한 자리에서는 소리가 신경 쓰일 수 있어요.
explain_en: Saying '후루룩 마시다/먹다', with the adverb '후루룩' plus another verb, sounds more natural than the verb form. It is used for quickly drawing in noodles or broth with a sound. In a quiet place, the noise can be noticeable.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 키가 후리후리해서 어떤 옷도 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: That actor is tall and slim, so any outfit suits him.
My younger sibling has a tall, slim figure with long legs.
My father has been tall and slim since he was young.
I'm not tall and slim, but I'm healthy.

examples.ko: 후리후리하게 자란 아들이 벌써 저보다 커요.
examples.en: My son, who has grown up tall and slim, is already taller than me.
A tall, slim, stylish person who looked like a model walked past.

explain: '키가 크다'에 '날씬하다'는 느낌이 더해진 말이라, 키만 큰 사람보다 늘씬한 체형에 어울려요. 비슷한 '훤칠하다'는 키뿐 아니라 시원스럽게 잘생긴 느낌까지 있어요. 주로 사람의 키와 몸에 쓰는 칭찬이에요.
explain_en: It adds a slim feel to being tall, so it fits a lean build rather than just height. The similar '훤칠하다' also carries a sense of looking clean-cut and handsome. It is mostly a compliment about a person's height and body.

examples.ko: 후미진 골목이라 밤에는 혼자 가기 무서워요.
examples.en: It's a secluded alley, so I'm scared to go alone at night.
That restaurant is tucked away, so it's hard to find.
The road is a bit out of the way, but I like that it's quiet.
Even though the shop is tucked away, customers keep coming.
The mountains are secluded and quiet, so they're good for resting.
The neighborhood that used to be tucked away is now very famous.

explain: 길, 골목, 마을처럼 구석진 곳에 써요. '외지다'가 중심에서 멀리 떨어진 느낌이라면, '후미지다'는 으슥하고 안쪽으로 들어간 느낌이 더 강해요. '후미진 골목'처럼 조금 어둡고 쓸쓸한 분위기로 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It describes places tucked into a corner, such as roads, alleys and villages. '외지다' feels far from the center, while '후미지다' feels more shadowy and set back inside. It is often used for a slightly dim, lonely atmosphere, as in '후미진 골목'.

examples.en: After the movie ended, I was curious about what happened next.
My senior told me what happened after that incident.
I closed the book only after reading the epilogue too.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 후일담은 인터뷰에서 처음 공개됐어요.
examples.en: The story of what happened to that singer afterward was first revealed in an interview.
The novel ends with an epilogue about the main character.

examples.ko: 감독이 말해 준 촬영 후일담도 정말 웃겨요.
examples.en: The behind-the-scenes stories the director told about filming are really funny too.

explain: 사건이나 작품이 끝난 뒤의 이야기를 말해요. 영화, 소설, 방송에서 '그 뒤에는 어떻게 됐는지'를 보여 줄 때 자주 어울려요. 촬영이나 제작 뒷이야기를 말할 때도 쓰고, 말로는 '뒷이야기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means the story of what happened after an event or a work ended. It fits movies, novels and broadcasts that show what became of things afterward. It is also used for behind-the-scenes stories, and in speech people also say '뒷이야기'.

examples.en: I got caught in the rain and my clothes became soggy and limp.
I'm embarrassed to go out looking so shabby.
I worked all day, so my shirt is all rumpled and limp.

examples.ko: 후줄근하게 입고 다니지 말고 좀 단정하게 입어요.
examples.en: Don't go around dressed sloppily; dress a bit neatly.
It's an old T-shirt, so it's saggy, but it's comfortable.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖어 후줄근해진 모습으로 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview looking drenched in sweat and bedraggled.

explain: 옷이나 사람의 모습이 젖거나 오래 입어서 축 처지고 단정하지 않을 때 써요. 좋은 말이 아니라서 남에게 직접 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 자기 모습을 말할 때는 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It describes clothes or a person's look that is limp, drooping and untidy from being wet or worn a long time. It is not a nice word, so saying it directly to someone can be rude. It is natural when describing your own appearance.

examples.ko: 성격은 타고나기도 하지만 후천적 노력도 중요해요.
examples.en: Personality is partly inborn, but acquired effort matters too.

examples.ko: 이 병은 후천적으로 생기는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: This illness often develops later in life rather than being present from birth.

examples.ko: 재능은 후천적인 훈련으로 얼마든지 키울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can develop talent through training, as much as you like.
That ability is acquired, so it improves with practice.

examples.ko: 알레르기는 선천적일 수도 있고 후천적일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: An allergy can be inborn or it can be acquired later.
I think all of my habits were acquired, not inborn.

explain: '선천적'의 반대말이에요. 태어난 뒤에 경험이나 환경, 노력으로 생긴 것을 말할 때 써요. '후천적 요인'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰기도 하고, '후천적이다', '후천적으로 생기다'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '선천적' (inborn). It refers to things that develop after birth through experience, environment or effort. It can come before a noun, as in '후천적 요인', or be used as '후천적이다' or '후천적으로 생기다'.

examples.en: It's the rainy season, so the room feels muggy.
When I turned off the air conditioner, it quickly became stuffy.
In sultry weather, I don't even have an appetite.

examples.ko: 버스 안이 너무 후텁지근해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: It was so stuffy inside the bus that I opened the window.
It's sultry, but there's a breeze, so it's bearable.

examples.ko: 비가 그친 뒤에 더 후텁지근하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It feels even more sticky and hot after the rain stops.

explain: 덥기만 한 것이 아니라 습기 때문에 공기가 끈끈하고 답답할 때 써요. '무덥다'와 비슷한 상황에 쓰고, 방 안이나 버스 안처럼 막힌 공간의 공기에도 잘 어울려요. 그냥 '덥다'와 달리 불쾌한 느낌이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when the air feels sticky and oppressive from humidity, not just hot. It fits situations similar to '무덥다' and works well for the air in closed spaces like a room or a bus. Unlike plain '덥다', it carries an unpleasant feeling.

examples.ko: 후환이 두려워서 아무도 말을 못 해요.
examples.en: Everyone is afraid of the consequences, so nobody speaks up.
I sorted it out carefully so as not to leave any trouble behind.
There won't be any trouble later, so don't worry.
A small lie came back as big trouble.
I want to finish this cleanly without any trouble afterward.

examples.ko: 그렇게 하면 후환도 만만치 않을 거예요.
examples.en: If you do that, the aftermath won't be easy either.

explain: 어떤 일을 한 뒤에 나중에 닥칠 나쁜 결과나 골칫거리를 말해요. 보통 '후환이 두렵다', '후환이 남다', '후환이 없다'처럼 써요. '후유증'은 병이나 사고의 뒤탈이고, '후환'은 행동 때문에 생길 수 있는 문제에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It refers to bad consequences or trouble that may come later because of something you did. It is usually used as '후환이 두렵다', '후환이 남다' or '후환이 없다'. '후유증' is the aftereffect of an illness or accident, while '후환' is closer to problems caused by an action.

examples.ko: 난로 덕분에 방 안에 훈기가 돌아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the heater, warmth is spreading through the room.
The room was filled with warm air.
I felt the warmth rising from the soup pot.
With nobody at home, there's no warmth either.
The warmth made me drowsy.

examples.ko: 훈기 있는 방에서 차를 마시니 좋아요.
examples.en: It feels nice to drink tea in a warm room.

explain: 따뜻하게 퍼지는 기운을 말해요. 날씨보다 방 안, 음식, 사람들이 모인 자리에서 느껴지는 따뜻함에 잘 어울려요. 비슷한 '온기'는 일상에서 쓰기 쉽고, '훈훈하다'와 같은 느낌의 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to warmth that spreads out. It fits warmth felt in a room, in food or where people gather, more than in the weather. The similar '온기' is easy to use in daily speech, and '훈기' shares the feeling of '훈훈하다'.

examples.en: My younger brother enlists as a recruit next month.
The recruits have been running around the field since morning.

examples.ko: 훈련병은 외출을 마음대로 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Recruits can't go out whenever they like.

examples.ko: 아들이 훈련병 때 쓴 편지를 아직 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: I still have the letter my son wrote when he was a recruit.
I looked up the address to send a letter to a recruit.
Recruits also get some free time on weekends.

explain: 입대한 뒤 훈련소에서 기본 훈련을 받는 동안 부르는 말이에요. 훈련을 마치고 부대에 가면 더 이상 훈련병이라고 부르지 않아요. 군대 이야기에서 '입대'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the term for someone receiving basic training at a training center after enlisting. After finishing training and going to a unit, the person is no longer called a '훈련병'. It often appears alongside '입대' in talk about the military.

examples.ko: 바둑을 두는데 옆에서 자꾸 훈수를 둬요.
examples.en: Someone beside me keeps giving advice while I play baduk.

examples.ko: 남의 일에 훈수 두지 말고 가만히 있어요.
examples.en: Don't butt in with advice on other people's business; just stay quiet.

examples.ko: 훈수가 도움이 될 때도 있지만 때로는 방해돼요.
examples.en: Unasked advice can sometimes help, but sometimes it gets in the way.

examples.ko: 친구의 훈수 덕분에 문제를 쉽게 풀었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my friend's tip, I solved the problem easily.

examples.ko: 게임할 때 옆에서 하는 훈수는 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Backseat advice from beside me while I play a game doesn't help.
There were so many people giving advice that the game got noisy.

explain: 원래 바둑이나 장기에서 구경하는 사람이 수를 알려 주는 일을 말하는데, 지금은 남의 일에 이래라저래라 말하는 것에도 써요. 보통 '훈수를 두다'라고 해요. 도와주는 느낌보다 참견하는 느낌이 들 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It originally meant a spectator suggesting moves in baduk or janggi, and now it is also used for telling others what to do in their affairs. It is usually said as '훈수를 두다'. It often feels more like meddling than helping.

examples.ko: 교장 선생님의 훈화가 너무 길어서 다리가 아팠어요.
examples.en: The principal's talk was so long that my legs hurt.
Every Monday morning we listen to an address on the playground.
Today's address was about not wasting time.
The talks are fine, but I wish they were short.

examples.ko: 훈화에 나온 이야기가 오래 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: The story from the address stays in my memory for a long time.
I tried hard not to doze off during the address.

explain: 주로 학교에서 교장 선생님이 학생들에게 들려주는 교훈적인 말씀을 가리켜요. 보통 '훈화 말씀'이라고 하고, 길면 잔소리처럼 느껴지기도 해요. 회사나 군대에서도 윗사람의 교훈적인 말에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It mainly refers to the moral talk a principal gives students at school. People usually say '훈화 말씀', and when it is long it can feel like nagging. It can also be used for a superior's moral talk at a company or in the military.

examples.ko: 오늘 힘들었던 일은 훌훌 털어 버려요.
examples.en: Let's shake off everything that was hard today.
The birds were startled and flitted away.
I brushed the dust off my clothes and got up.

examples.ko: 걱정은 훌훌 던져 버리고 여행을 떠났어요.
examples.en: I tossed my worries aside and left on a trip.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 걸 정리하고 훌훌 떠났어요.
examples.en: He wrapped everything up and left without looking back.
Autumn leaves flutter away in the wind.

explain: 털다, 던지다, 떠나다처럼 무언가를 가볍게 떨치거나 미련 없이 보내는 동작과 자주 함께 써요. 가볍게 날리는 모습에도 쓰지만, 마음의 짐을 내려놓는 느낌으로 많이 말해요. '훌훌 털다'는 걱정이나 힘든 기억을 잊을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.example: 시험 결과는 잊고 훌훌 털고 다시 시작해요.
phrases.en: Forget the test result, shake it off and start again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼지를 터는 뜻이 아니라, 걱정이나 나쁜 기억을 미련 없이 떨쳐 내는 표현이에요. 위로하거나 다짐할 때 자주 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about brushing off dust; it means shedding worries or bad memories without lingering. It fits comforting someone or making a resolution.

explain_en: It often goes with verbs like 털다, 던지다 and 떠나다, for shaking something off or letting it go lightly with no lingering. It can also describe things fluttering lightly, but it is often used for putting down an emotional burden. '훌훌 털다' is an expression for letting go of worries or hard memories.

examples.en: That actor is tall and handsome.

examples.ko: 훤칠한 청년이 가게 문을 열고 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A tall, good-looking young man opened the shop door and came in.
My son has grown up tall and good-looking, and it's nice to see.
I heard the groom is tall and handsome, and has a good personality too.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선생님은 훤칠해서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The new teacher stands out because he's tall and good-looking.

examples.ko: 저는 훤칠하지는 않아도 인상이 좋다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: I may not be tall and striking, but people say I have a good impression.

explain: 키가 크면서 모습이 시원스럽고 보기 좋을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. '후리후리하다'는 키 크고 날씬한 몸을 말하고, '훤칠하다'는 거기에 잘생긴 느낌까지 더해져요. 주로 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who is tall and looks clean-cut and pleasing. '후리후리하다' describes a tall, slim body, while '훤칠하다' adds a handsome feel. It is used mainly for people.
